## Method

The [United States Census](United_States_Census "United States Census") counts the persons residing in the [United States](United_States "United States") including [citizens](Citizenship "Citizenship"), non-citizen [permanent residents](Permanent_residence_(United_States) "Permanent residence (United States)") and non-citizen long-term visitors.[[2]](List_of_U.S._states_and_territories_by_population#cite_note-2) Civilian and military federal employees serving abroad and their dependents are counted in their home state.[[3]](List_of_U.S._states_and_territories_by_population#cite_note-3)

## Electoral apportionment

Every 10 years, the [U.S. Census Bureau](U.S._Census_Bureau "U.S. Census Bureau") is charged with making an actual count of all residents by state and territory. The accuracy of this count is then tested after the fact, and sometimes statistically significant undercounts or overcounts occur. ### House of Representatives

Based on this decennial census, each state is allocated a portion of the 435 fixed seats in the [United States House of Representatives](United_States_House_of_Representatives "United States House of Representatives") (until the early 20th century, the apportionment process generally increased the size of the House based on the results of the census until the size of the House was capped by the [Reapportionment Act of 1929](Reapportionment_Act_of_1929 "Reapportionment Act of 1929")), with each state guaranteed at least one Representative. **Washington**[[lower-alpha 1]](Washington_(state)#cite_note-4) (/ˈwɑːʃɪŋtən/ [](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/transcoded/7/71/En-us-Washington.ogg/En-us-Washington.ogg.mp3)i), officially the **State of Washington**,[[4]](Washington_(state)#cite_note-:1-5) is a [state](U.S._state "U.S. state") in the [Pacific Northwest](Northwestern_United_States "Northwestern United States") region of the [Western United States](Western_United_States "Western United States"). Named for [George Washington](George_Washington "George Washington")—the first [U.S. president](President_of_the_United_States "President of the United States")—the state was formed from the western part of the [Washington Territory](Washington_Territory "Washington Territory"), which was ceded by the [British Empire](British_Empire "British Empire") in 1846, by the [Oregon Treaty](Oregon_Treaty "Oregon Treaty") in the settlement of the [Oregon boundary dispute](Oregon_boundary_dispute "Oregon boundary dispute"). The state is bordered on the west by the Pacific Ocean, <Oregon> to the south, <Idaho> to the east, and the [Canadian province](Provinces_and_territories_of_Canada "Provinces and territories of Canada") of [British Columbia](British_Columbia "British Columbia") to the north. It was admitted to the Union as the 42nd state in 1889. [Olympia](Olympia%2C_Washington "Olympia, Washington") is the [state capital](List_of_capitals_in_the_United_States "List of capitals in the United States"). The state's most populous city is <Seattle>.

Washington is the [18th-largest state](List_of_U.S._states_and_territories_by_area "List of U.S. states and territories by area"), with an area of 71,362 square miles (184,830 km2), and the [13th-most populous](List_of_U.S._states_and_territories_by_population "List of U.S. states and territories by population") state, with more than 7.7 million people.[[5]](Washington_(state)#cite_note-6) The majority of Washington's residents live in the [Seattle metropolitan area](Seattle_metropolitan_area "Seattle metropolitan area"), the center of transportation, business, and industry on [Puget Sound](Puget_Sound "Puget Sound"),[[6]](Washington_(state)#cite_note-7)[[7]](Washington_(state)#cite_note-8) an inlet of the Pacific Ocean consisting of numerous islands, deep [fjords](Fjord "Fjord") and bays carved out by glaciers.
